title: CTS Administration & Leadership — Unit 8: Facilities, Legal Matters, and Risk Management

blocks.en: 📖 Administration & Leadership — Unit 8: Facilities, Legal Matters, and Risk Management
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Administración y Liderazgo — Unidad 8: Instalaciones, asuntos legales y gestión de riesgos

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Let all things be done decently and in order." — 1 Corinthians 14:40 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Hágase todo decentemente y con orden." — 1 Corintios 14:40 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction — "Decently and in Order" Reaches the Building
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — "Decentemente y con orden" alcanza el edificio

blocks.en: Some pastors imagine that the spiritual part of ministry is the sermon and the prayer meeting, while the building, the paperwork, and the insurance are a lower and dirtier business, beneath a man of God. That instinct is a mistake, and a costly one. The same Spirit who inspired "Let all things be done decently and in order" (1 Corinthians 14:40) was not speaking only of the worship service. Order in the house of God reaches all the way to the roof that does not leak, the door that locks, the records that are honest, and the children who go home as safe as they came. A church can lose in a single afternoon — through a fire, a lawsuit, or a scandal of negligence — what it took a generation of faithful preaching to build. This unit is about guarding that. It is not worldly to be careful. It is faithful. The leader who despises these "small" things has not risen above administration; he has simply left the back door of the church standing wide open.
blocks.es_reference: Algunos pastores imaginan que la parte espiritual del ministerio es el sermón y la reunión de oración, mientras que el edificio, el papeleo y el seguro son un asunto inferior y más sucio, por debajo de un hombre de Dios. Ese instinto es un error, y uno costoso. El mismo Espíritu que inspiró "hágase todo decentemente y con orden" (1 Corintios 14:40) no hablaba solo del culto. El orden en la casa de Dios alcanza hasta el techo que no gotea, la puerta que cierra con llave, los registros que son honestos, y los niños que vuelven a casa tan seguros como llegaron. Una iglesia puede perder en una sola tarde — por un incendio, una demanda o un escándalo de negligencia — lo que tomó una generación de predicación fiel construir. Esta unidad trata de guardar eso. No es mundano ser cuidadoso. Es fiel. El líder que desprecia estas cosas "pequeñas" no se ha elevado por encima de la administración; sencillamente ha dejado la puerta trasera de la iglesia abierta de par en par.

blocks.en: I. The House of God Deserves Care
blocks.es_reference: I. La casa de Dios merece cuidado

blocks.en: Begin with a simple conviction: the place where God's people gather is not nothing. Under the old covenant, God gave page after page of detailed instruction for the care of the tabernacle and then the temple — who carried what, who cleaned what, who guarded the doors, how the furnishings were kept. The Levites had whole careers in what we would call facilities administration, and God counted it holy work. When the temple fell into disrepair, godly kings like Joash and Josiah made its repair a spiritual priority, gathering funds and hiring honest workmen to restore the house of the Lord.
blocks.es_reference: Comience con una convicción sencilla: el lugar donde el pueblo de Dios se reúne no es nada. Bajo el antiguo pacto, Dios dio página tras página de instrucción detallada para el cuidado del tabernáculo y luego del templo — quién cargaba qué, quién limpiaba qué, quién guardaba las puertas, cómo se mantenían los muebles. Los levitas tenían carreras enteras en lo que llamaríamos administración de instalaciones, y Dios lo contó obra santa. Cuando el templo cayó en mal estado, reyes piadosos como Joás y Josías hicieron de su reparación una prioridad espiritual, recogiendo fondos y contratando obreros honestos para restaurar la casa del Señor.

blocks.en: Now we must be careful here, because the building is not the church — the people are the temple of the Holy Spirit now, not the bricks. But the place where the flock gathers to worship, to learn, and to be cared for is a tool God has given for the work, and a steward does not let the Master's tools rust and rot. A roof that leaks over the heads of worshipers, a dirty nursery, a building falling apart from neglect — these preach a sermon of their own, and it is not a good one. To care for the place where the people gather is to honor the people who gather there and the God they gather to worship. Keep the house in good order. It is part of doing all things decently.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora debemos tener cuidado aquí, porque el edificio no es la iglesia — el pueblo es el templo del Espíritu Santo ahora, no los ladrillos. Pero el lugar donde la grey se reúne para adorar, para aprender y para ser cuidada es una herramienta que Dios ha dado para la obra, y un mayordomo no deja que las herramientas del Amo se oxiden y se pudran. Un techo que gotea sobre las cabezas de los adoradores, una cuna sucia, un edificio que se cae a pedazos por abandono — estos predican un sermón propio, y no es uno bueno. Cuidar el lugar donde el pueblo se reúne es honrar al pueblo que se reúne allí y al Dios que se reúnen a adorar. Mantenga la casa en buen orden. Es parte de hacer todo decentemente.

blocks.en: It is not worldly to be careful. It is faithful.
blocks.es_reference: No es mundano ser cuidadoso. Es fiel.

blocks.en: II. Render to Caesar: The Church and the Law
blocks.es_reference: II. Dad al César: la iglesia y la ley

blocks.en: Now to a harder subject, where many sincere leaders stumble out of ignorance. The church does not exist in a legal vacuum. It sits inside a nation with laws, and the New Testament is unambiguous about the believer's posture toward those laws. "Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God" (Romans 13:1). And the Lord Himself: "Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matthew 22:21). Paul presses the practical edge: "Render therefore to all their due: taxes to whom taxes are due, customs to whom customs" (Romans 13:7).
blocks.es_reference: Ahora a un tema más difícil, donde muchos líderes sinceros tropiezan por ignorancia. La iglesia no existe en un vacío legal. Está dentro de una nación con leyes, y el Nuevo Testamento es inequívoco sobre la postura del creyente hacia esas leyes. "Sométase toda persona a las potestades superiores; porque no hay potestad sino de Dios" (Romanos 13:1). Y el Señor mismo: "Dad pues a César lo que es de César, y a Dios lo que es de Dios" (Mateo 22:21). Pablo aprieta el filo práctico: "Pagad a todos lo que debéis: al que tributo, tributo; al que impuesto, impuesto" (Romanos 13:7).

blocks.en: Hear this clearly, brother. Where the law of the land does not command you to sin nor forbid you to obey God, the church is to be the most law-abiding body in the community, not the most evasive. That means the church should be properly registered and recognized under the laws of its nation. It means the church keeps honest records and meets its legal obligations — the employment rules for those it pays, the permits for what it builds, whatever the civil authority justly requires. A church that cuts legal corners "to save money" or "because we are spiritual" is not being spiritual; it is disobeying a direct command of Scripture and setting a trap for its own future. Of course, when human law collides with the law of God — when Caesar demands what belongs to God alone — we must, with the apostles, "obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29). But that line is crossed far more rarely than the lazy leader pretends. In all the ordinary business of legal compliance, render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and let the church's paperwork be as honest as its preaching.
blocks.es_reference: Oiga esto con claridad, hermano. Donde la ley de la tierra no le ordena pecar ni le prohíbe obedecer a Dios, la iglesia ha de ser el cuerpo más cumplidor de la ley en la comunidad, no el más evasivo. Eso significa que la iglesia debe estar debidamente registrada y reconocida bajo las leyes de su nación. Significa que la iglesia lleva registros honestos y cumple sus obligaciones legales — las reglas de empleo para quienes paga, los permisos para lo que construye, lo que la autoridad civil justamente requiera. Una iglesia que recorta esquinas legales "para ahorrar dinero" o "porque somos espirituales" no está siendo espiritual; está desobedeciendo un mandato directo de la Escritura y poniéndose una trampa para su propio futuro. Por supuesto, cuando la ley humana choca con la ley de Dios — cuando el César exige lo que pertenece solo a Dios — debemos, con los apóstoles, "obedecer a Dios antes que a los hombres" (Hechos 5:29). Pero esa línea se cruza mucho más rara vez de lo que finge el líder perezoso. En todo el asunto ordinario del cumplimiento legal, dad al César lo que es del César, y que el papeleo de la iglesia sea tan honesto como su predicación.

blocks.en: "Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's." — Matthew 22:21 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Dad pues a César lo que es de César, y a Dios lo que es de Dios." — Mateo 22:21 (RVG)

blocks.en: III. A Good Testimony with Outsiders
blocks.es_reference: III. Buen testimonio con los de afuera

blocks.en: There is a spiritual reason for this care that runs deeper than avoiding trouble. Paul lists the qualifications of an overseer and then adds one that surprises us: "Moreover he must have a good testimony among those who are outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil" (1 Timothy 3:7). The reputation of the church and its leaders before the watching unbelieving community is a gospel matter. The neighbors, the officials, the businesses around the church — they are forming a judgment about Christ from how His people conduct their affairs.
blocks.es_reference: Hay una razón espiritual para este cuidado que corre más hondo que evitar problemas. Pablo enumera las cualidades de un obispo y luego añade una que nos sorprende: "También es necesario que tenga buen testimonio de los de afuera, para que no caiga en descrédito y en lazo del diablo" (1 Timoteo 3:7). La reputación de la iglesia y de sus líderes ante la comunidad incrédula que observa es un asunto del evangelio. Los vecinos, los funcionarios, los negocios alrededor de la iglesia — están formando un juicio acerca de Cristo a partir de cómo su pueblo conduce sus asuntos.

blocks.en: When a church pays its debts on time, honors its agreements, keeps its property in decent order, and deals with the authorities honestly, it adorns the gospel and removes an obstacle between its neighbors and Christ. When a church is known for unpaid bills, broken promises, a building in ruins, and corners cut with the law, it hangs a stumbling block in the doorway and hands the devil a snare. The world will forgive the church many things, but it will not fail to notice hypocrisy in the handling of money and obligations. So administer the church's external affairs the way a missionary administers his own — knowing the outsiders are always watching, and that a good testimony among them is worth guarding as carefully as any doctrine.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando una iglesia paga sus deudas a tiempo, honra sus acuerdos, mantiene su propiedad en orden decente, y trata con las autoridades honestamente, adorna el evangelio y quita un obstáculo entre sus vecinos y Cristo. Cuando una iglesia es conocida por cuentas sin pagar, promesas rotas, un edificio en ruinas y esquinas recortadas con la ley, cuelga un tropiezo en la entrada y le entrega al diablo un lazo. El mundo le perdonará a la iglesia muchas cosas, pero no dejará de notar la hipocresía en el manejo del dinero y las obligaciones. Así que administre los asuntos externos de la iglesia como un misionero administra los suyos — sabiendo que los de afuera siempre observan, y que un buen testimonio entre ellos vale la pena guardarse con tanto cuidado como cualquier doctrina.

blocks.en: IV. The Prudent See Danger: Risk Management
blocks.es_reference: IV. El prudente ve el peligro: la gestión de riesgos

blocks.en: Now to the discipline the world calls risk management, which Scripture simply calls prudence. "A prudent man foresees evil and hides himself; but the simple pass on and are punished" (Proverbs 22:3). The wise leader looks down the road and asks, before it happens, "What could go wrong here, and what would we do?" The foolish leader never asks until the disaster is already on top of him, and by then it is too late.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora a la disciplina que el mundo llama gestión de riesgos, que la Escritura sencillamente llama prudencia. "El avisado ve el mal, y se esconde; mas los simples pasan, y reciben el daño" (Proverbios 22:3). El líder sabio mira camino abajo y pregunta, antes de que suceda: "¿Qué podría salir mal aquí, y qué haríamos?" El líder necio nunca pregunta hasta que el desastre le cae encima, y entonces ya es tarde.

blocks.en: This is not a lack of faith; it is the very wisdom God commends. "Be diligent to know the state of your flocks, and attend to your herds" (Proverbs 27:23) — the shepherd's careful, regular attention to the real condition of what is in his care. Remember Nehemiah from Unit 3: when the threat came, he did not only pray; he set a guard. Faith and a watch go together. So the prudent church looks ahead to foreseeable dangers and prepares: it carries the insurance a responsible steward would carry, so that an accident or fire does not destroy the work; it keeps its building genuinely safe — the wiring, the exits, the stairs, the kitchen; it sets aside money against the lean year instead of spending every peso as it comes. None of this betrays a lack of trust in God. The God who fed Joseph's Egypt through seven years of famine by means of seven years of storing grain is the same God who tells the prudent to see danger coming. Trust God fully — and check the smoke detectors.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es falta de fe; es la misma sabiduría que Dios encomia. "Sé diligente en conocer el estado de tus ovejas, y mira con cuidado por tus rebaños" (Proverbios 27:23) — la atención cuidadosa y regular del pastor a la condición real de lo que está a su cuidado. Recuerde a Nehemías de la Unidad 3: cuando vino la amenaza, no solo oró; puso guardia. La fe y una guardia van juntas. Así que la iglesia prudente mira hacia adelante a los peligros previsibles y se prepara: lleva el seguro que un mayordomo responsable llevaría, para que un accidente o incendio no destruya la obra; mantiene su edificio genuinamente seguro — la instalación eléctrica, las salidas, las escaleras, la cocina; aparta dinero contra el año de escasez en vez de gastar cada peso conforme llega. Nada de esto traiciona una falta de confianza en Dios. El Dios que alimentó el Egipto de José a través de siete años de escasez por medio de siete años de almacenar grano es el mismo Dios que dice al prudente que vea venir el peligro. Confíe en Dios plenamente — y revise los detectores de humo.

blocks.en: "A prudent man foresees evil and hides himself; but the simple pass on and are punished." — Proverbs 22:3 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "El avisado ve el mal, y se esconde; mas los simples pasan, y reciben el daño." — Proverbios 22:3 (RVG)

blocks.en: V. Guarding the Vulnerable
blocks.es_reference: V. Guardar a los vulnerables

blocks.en: Of all the risks a church must manage, one rises so far above the rest that it deserves its own place, and I will speak of it without flinching: the protection of children and the vulnerable. Our Lord reserved some of His most terrible words for those who would harm a child: "whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to sin, it would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were drowned in the depth of the sea" (Matthew 18:6). The church must be the safest place a child can be, never a place where a predator can hide behind a smile and a Bible.
blocks.es_reference: De todos los riesgos que una iglesia debe gestionar, uno se eleva tan por encima del resto que merece su propio lugar, y hablaré de él sin titubear: la protección de los niños y los vulnerables. Nuestro Señor reservó algunas de sus palabras más terribles para quienes harían daño a un niño: "cualquiera que hiciere tropezar a alguno de estos pequeños que creen en mí, mejor le fuera que se le colgase al cuello una piedra de molino de asno, y que se le anegase en lo profundo del mar" (Mateo 18:6). La iglesia debe ser el lugar más seguro donde un niño pueda estar, nunca un lugar donde un depredador pueda esconderse tras una sonrisa y una Biblia.

blocks.en: This is not cynicism about people; it is love for the lambs, and it is simple obedience to a Shepherd who counts them precious. So the wise church puts real protections in place and does not apologize for them: it screens those who work with children rather than handing access to anyone who volunteers; it follows sensible rules so that no worker is ever alone and unaccountable with a child, which protects the children and also protects the innocent worker from a false accusation; it takes any concern with complete seriousness. The leader who finds these measures "unspiritual" or "suspicious" has not understood what is at stake. A single predator admitted through carelessness can destroy children's lives and the church's testimony in one blow. Guard the vulnerable as the Chief Shepherd guards His lambs — deliberately, vigilantly, and without shame. This is one watch the leader must never relax.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es cinismo acerca de las personas; es amor por los corderos, y es simple obediencia a un Pastor que los cuenta preciosos. Así que la iglesia sabia pone protecciones reales en su lugar y no se disculpa por ellas: investiga a quienes trabajan con niños en vez de entregar el acceso a cualquiera que se ofrezca; sigue reglas sensatas para que ningún obrero esté jamás solo y sin rendición de cuentas con un niño, lo cual protege a los niños y también protege al obrero inocente de una acusación falsa; toma cualquier inquietud con completa seriedad. El líder que halla estas medidas "poco espirituales" o "sospechosas" no ha entendido lo que está en juego. Un solo depredador admitido por descuido puede destruir vidas de niños y el testimonio de la iglesia de un solo golpe. Guarde a los vulnerables como el Príncipe de los pastores guarda a sus corderos — deliberadamente, vigilantemente y sin vergüenza. Esta es una guardia que el líder nunca debe relajar.

blocks.en: VI. Wise as Serpents, Innocent as Doves
blocks.es_reference: VI. Prudentes como serpientes, sencillos como palomas

blocks.en: Perhaps you feel a tension in all of this, and it is worth naming. Does this careful, legal, insured, screened, locked-and-guarded way of operating sit uneasily beside a life of faith? Are we trusting God or trusting our precautions? The Lord Himself dissolved the tension in a single sentence when He sent His disciples into a dangerous world: "be wise as serpents and harmless as doves" (Matthew 10:16). Both at once. The dove's innocence without the serpent's prudence is naive, and it gets the flock hurt. The serpent's prudence without the dove's innocence is mere worldly cunning. The faithful leader holds both.
blocks.es_reference: Quizá sienta una tensión en todo esto, y vale la pena nombrarla. ¿Acaso esta manera de operar —cuidadosa, legal, asegurada, investigada, con cerradura y guardia— choca con una vida de fe? ¿Estamos confiando en Dios o confiando en nuestras precauciones? El Señor mismo disolvió la tensión en una sola oración cuando envió a sus discípulos a un mundo peligroso: "sed pues prudentes como serpientes, y sencillos como palomas" (Mateo 10:16). Ambas a la vez. La inocencia de la paloma sin la prudencia de la serpiente es ingenua, y lastima a la grey. La prudencia de la serpiente sin la inocencia de la paloma es mera astucia mundana. El líder fiel sostiene ambas.

blocks.en: So none of this prudence is permission for the church to become a cold, suspicious, lawyer-run institution that has lost its soul. The building serves the ministry; it is not the ministry. The policies protect the flock; they are not the flock. The goal is never to turn the house of God into a fortress of rules, but to remove every needless danger and reproach so that the real work — the preaching, the shepherding, the gospel — can go forward unhindered. Be innocent in heart and shrewd in practice. Trust God with everything, and also lock the door, pay the tax, insure the roof, screen the worker, and keep the records honest. That is not a smaller faith. It is faith doing all things decently and in order, down to the very foundations.
blocks.es_reference: Así que nada de esta prudencia es permiso para que la iglesia se vuelva una institución fría, sospechosa, manejada por abogados, que ha perdido su alma. El edificio sirve al ministerio; no es el ministerio. Las políticas protegen a la grey; no son la grey. La meta nunca es convertir la casa de Dios en una fortaleza de reglas, sino quitar todo peligro y oprobio innecesario para que la obra verdadera — la predicación, el pastoreo, el evangelio — pueda avanzar sin estorbo. Sea inocente de corazón y sagaz en la práctica. Confíe en Dios con todo, y también cierre la puerta con llave, pague el impuesto, asegure el techo, investigue al obrero, y mantenga honestos los registros. Eso no es una fe más pequeña. Es la fe haciendo todo decentemente y con orden, hasta los mismos cimientos.

mc.stem: According to the introduction, the instinct that treats buildings, paperwork, and insurance as 'beneath' a man of God is:
options: A mistake, and a costly one
mc.why: That instinct is a costly mistake; order in God's house reaches all the way to the roof, the locks, and the records.

mc.stem: The verse that frames the whole unit, showing order reaches beyond the worship service, is:
mc.why: "Let all things be done decently and in order" (1 Cor 14:40) governs the building too, not only the service.

mc.stem: How long can it take a church to lose what a generation of faithful preaching built?
mc.why: A fire, a lawsuit, or a scandal of negligence can undo in one afternoon what took a generation to build.

mc.stem: The relationship between the building and the church is best stated as:
options: The building is a God-given tool for the work, not the church itself
The building is more important than the people
mc.why: The people are the temple now; the building is a tool a steward keeps in good order, not the church itself.

mc.stem: Joash and Josiah are cited as kings who:
options: Made repairing the house of the Lord a spiritual priority
mc.why: Godly kings treated repairing the disrepaired temple as spiritual work, gathering funds and honest workmen.

mc.stem: Where human law does not command sin or forbid obedience to God, the church should be:
options: The most law-abiding body in the community
The most evasive body in the community
mc.why: Romans 13 and Matthew 22:21 require the church to be the most law-abiding body, not the most evasive.

mc.stem: "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's" was spoken by:
mc.why: Jesus Himself said it (Matthew 22:21); Paul presses the practical edge in Romans 13:7.

mc.stem: The only time the church should NOT comply with the civil authority is when:
options: The law collides with the law of God, commanding sin or forbidding obedience to God
The leader disagrees with the law
mc.why: Only when Caesar demands what belongs to God alone do we 'obey God rather than men' (Acts 5:29) — rarely.

mc.stem: The surprising overseer qualification in 1 Timothy 3:7 is that he must have:
options: A good testimony among those outside
mc.why: A leader must have a good testimony among outsiders, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

mc.stem: When a church pays debts late, breaks promises, and cuts corners with the law, it:
options: Hangs a stumbling block in the doorway and hands the devil a snare
mc.why: Outsiders judge Christ by the church's conduct; hypocrisy in money and obligations becomes a stumbling block.

mc.stem: Proverbs 22:3 says the prudent man, unlike the simple, will:
mc.why: Risk management is biblical prudence: the prudent foresee evil and prepare; the simple pass on and are punished.

mc.stem: The unit argues that carrying insurance and keeping the building safe:
options: Is a waste of the Lord's money
Betrays a lack of trust in God
Does not betray a lack of trust in God, but is the prudence God commends
mc.why: The God who stored grain through Joseph for seven lean years commends seeing danger and preparing for it.

mc.stem: The example of Nehemiah (Unit 3) shows that faith and a guard:
options: Go together — he prayed and set a watch
mc.why: When threatened, Nehemiah did not only pray; he set a guard. Faith and a watch belong together.

mc.stem: Among all risks, the one the unit says rises so far above the rest it gets its own section is:
options: The protection of children and the vulnerable
mc.why: Christ's millstone warning (Matt 18:6) sets child protection above every other risk a church manages.

mc.stem: The 'two-adult' style rule (no worker alone and unaccountable with a child) protects:
options: Both the children and the innocent worker from false accusation
mc.why: Sensible rules guard the children and also shield the innocent worker from a false accusation.

mc.stem: A leader who calls child-protection measures 'unspiritual' or 'suspicious' has:
options: Not understood what is at stake
mc.why: A single predator admitted through carelessness can destroy children's lives and the testimony in one blow.

mc.stem: Jesus' instruction in Matthew 10:16 to His sent disciples was to be:
options: Wise as serpents and harmless as doves
Wise as owls and gentle as sheep
Bold as lions and meek as lambs
Quick as deer and strong as oxen
mc.why: Both at once: dove-innocence without serpent-prudence is naive; serpent-prudence without dove-innocence is mere cunning.

mc.stem: The danger named if prudence is taken too far is that the church becomes:
options: A cold, suspicious, lawyer-run institution that has lost its soul
mc.why: Policies protect the flock but are not the flock; the building serves the ministry but is not the ministry.

mc.stem: The proper purpose of all this prudence, the unit says, is to:
options: Remove needless danger and reproach so the real work can go forward unhindered
Turn the house of God into a fortress of rules
mc.why: The goal is to clear away needless danger and reproach so preaching, shepherding, and the gospel go unhindered.

mc.stem: The closing summary of the unit's posture toward faith and precaution is:
options: Take precautions instead of trusting God
Trust God instead of taking precautions
Trust God with everything, and also lock the door, pay the tax, insure the roof, and screen the worker
mc.why: It is not a smaller faith but faith doing all things decently and in order, down to the foundations.

sa.prompt: Explain how 'let all things be done decently and in order' (1 Cor 14:40) applies beyond the worship service.
sa.model: Order in the house of God is not confined to the worship service; it reaches the building, the roof that does not leak, the locked door, the honest record, and the children who go home safe. To be careful about these things is not worldly but faithful, because a church can lose in one afternoon what a generation of faithful preaching built. The leader who keeps the house in good order is simply obeying the same command decently and in order down to the foundations.

sa.prompt: What is the right relationship between the church building and the church itself?
sa.model: The building is not the church; the people are the temple of the Holy Spirit now, not the bricks. Yet the building is a God-given tool for the work, and a steward does not let the Master's tools rust and rot. To care for the place where the people gather is to honor both the people who gather and the God they worship, so the leader keeps the house in good order without ever confusing the tool with the church.

sa.prompt: Summarize the New Testament teaching on the church's posture toward civil law, including its limit.
sa.model: Scripture commands the church to be subject to the governing authorities and to render to Caesar what is Caesar's, paying taxes and customs honestly. Where the law does not command sin, the church should be the most law-abiding body in the community: properly registered, keeping honest records, and meeting its legal obligations. The single limit is that when human law collides with the law of God, commanding sin or forbidding obedience to God, we must obey God rather than men; but that line is crossed far more rarely than the lazy leader pretends, so we comply in all ordinary matters.

sa.prompt: Why does a church's reputation with outsiders matter, and what does 1 Timothy 3:7 add?
sa.model: A leader must have a good testimony among those who are outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. The reputation of the church before the watching unbelieving community is a gospel matter, because outsiders form their judgment about Christ from how His people conduct their affairs. A church that pays its debts, honors agreements, and deals honestly adorns the gospel; one known for broken promises and cut corners hangs a stumbling block and hands the devil a snare.

sa.prompt: Show how risk management is simply biblical prudence, using Proverbs 22:3 and 27:23.
sa.model: Risk management is what the world calls a discipline but Scripture calls prudence. The prudent man foresees evil and hides himself, while the simple pass on and are punished; the wise leader asks ahead of time what could go wrong and prepares. This is the same wisdom as being diligent to know the state of your flocks, the shepherd's careful attention to the real condition of what he guards. Foreseeing danger and preparing for it is not a failure of faith but the very wisdom God commends.

sa.prompt: Explain why preparing (insurance, savings, safety) does not betray a lack of trust in God.
sa.model: Preparing wisely does not betray a lack of trust in God; it is obedience to the God who commends prudence. The same God who fed Joseph's Egypt through seven years of famine by means of seven years of storing grain is the God who tells the prudent to see danger coming and prepare. So a church can trust God fully and still carry insurance, keep the building safe, and set aside savings against the lean year. Faith and faithful preparation are not rivals; trusting God and checking the smoke detectors belong together.

sa.prompt: Why does the protection of children rise above every other risk, and what guards should a church put in place?
sa.model: The protection of children and the vulnerable rises above every other risk because the Lord reserved His most terrible words — a millstone and the depth of the sea — for those who would harm a little one. The church must be the safest place a child can be, never a place where a predator hides behind a smile and a Bible. So the wise church screens those who work with children, follows rules so that no worker is ever alone and unaccountable with a child, and takes every concern seriously — guarding the vulnerable deliberately and without shame, a watch the leader must never relax.

sa.prompt: How do the two-adult/screening rules protect the worker as well as the child?
sa.model: Sensible rules that keep no worker ever alone and unaccountable with a child do double duty: they protect the child from harm, and they also protect the innocent worker from a false accusation. When a worker is never isolated with a child, there is accountability that shields a good servant if his integrity is ever questioned. Far from insulting faithful workers, these rules guard them; the leader who calls such protection suspicious has not understood what is at stake for the child or the innocent worker.

sa.prompt: Explain 'wise as serpents and harmless as doves' (Matt 10:16) as it applies to church administration.
sa.model: The Lord told His sent disciples to be wise as serpents and harmless as doves — both at once. The dove's innocence without the serpent's prudence is naive and gets the flock hurt; the serpent's prudence without the dove's innocence is mere worldly cunning. The faithful leader holds both: innocent in heart and shrewd in practice. He trusts God with everything and still locks the door, pays the tax, insures the roof, and screens the worker, refusing to choose between innocence and prudence.

sa.prompt: Guard against the misuse of prudence: what must facilities, policies, and law never become in the church?
sa.model: Prudence must never turn the church into a cold, suspicious, lawyer-run institution that has lost its soul. The building serves the ministry but is not the ministry; the policies protect the flock but are not the flock. The goal is never to make the house of God a fortress of rules, but to remove needless danger and reproach so the real work — preaching, shepherding, the gospel — can go forward unhindered. Keep prudence the servant of the work, never its master.
